title: Device administration with TACACS+
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Send router logins, EXEC authorization and command accounting to Cisco ISE over TACACS+.
purpose: Local accounts on every router don't scale and leave no central record of who changed what. This lab moves device logins to TACACS+ on ISE, so admins log in with central accounts, are authorized per command, and every command is logged. It covers AAA for device administration, a core SCOR topic.
scenario: The team wants one place to manage who can log in to network devices and to record every command they run. Cisco ISE at **10.10.99.10** has the Device Admin service turned on, and R1 is already added to it with the shared key **T4cacsKey**. Point R1 at ISE with TACACS+, and keep the local admin account as a fallback in case ISE can't be reached.
topology:
Admin PC ── R1 ──────── ISE 10.10.99.10 (TACACS+, TCP 49)
            local user: admin (fallback)
objectives: Turn on AAA and define ISE as a TACACS+ server
Group the server and build a login method list with local fallback
Authorize EXEC sessions and account for privilege 15 commands
Apply the method lists to the VTY lines

steps.title: Compare TACACS+ and RADIUS
steps.learn: Both protocols carry AAA traffic to a server such as ISE. **TACACS+** is the usual choice for **device administration**, and **RADIUS** for **network access** (802.1X, VPN, wireless).
steps.task: Pick the statements that are true of TACACS+.
steps.question: Which statements are true of TACACS+?

options.text: It encrypts the entire body of each packet.
It handles authentication, authorization and accounting separately, so commands can be authorized one by one.

options.why: Those are the RADIUS authentication and accounting ports.

options.text: It encrypts only the password field.
options.why: That's RADIUS. TACACS+ encrypts the whole payload.

steps.title: Turn on AAA and add the server
steps.learn: `aaa new-model` switches the device to the AAA framework. From then on, logins follow method lists instead of the old `login` and `password` line commands. Each TACACS+ server is defined once by name, with its address and shared key.
steps.task: Turn on the AAA model, then define a TACACS+ server named **ISE** at **10.10.99.10** with the key **T4cacsKey**.
steps.hint: `aaa new-model`, then `tacacs server ISE`, and inside it `address ipv4 10.10.99.10` and `key T4cacsKey`.

commands.note: AAA is on. Before you change the VTY lines, make sure a local account exists so you can't lock yourself out.
commands.explain: Turns on the AAA framework. Without it, the aaa commands that follow aren't available.
Defines a TACACS+ server and names it ISE.

commands.note: The key must match what ISE has for R1, character for character.
commands.explain: Sets the shared secret that encrypts traffic between the router and ISE. It must match ISE.

steps.title: Create a server group
steps.learn: Method lists point at **server groups**, not at single servers. A group can list several servers that are tried in order, and you can give it its own source interface.
steps.task: Create a TACACS+ server group named **ISE-GROUP** that contains the server **ISE**.
steps.hint: `aaa group server tacacs+ ISE-GROUP`, then `server name ISE`.

commands.explain: Creates a server group named ISE-GROUP that AAA method lists can point to.
Adds the ISE server to the group.

steps.title: Build the method lists
steps.learn:
A method list is tried left to right. The next method is used only when one is **unreachable**, not when it **rejects** the user. So with `group ISE-GROUP local`, the local account works only while ISE is down.

`if-authenticated` lets an authenticated user into EXEC mode even when no authorization server answers. Command accounting at level 15 records every privileged command.
steps.task: Create a login authentication list **VTY-AUTH** that uses **ISE-GROUP** and then **local**. Create an EXEC authorization list **VTY-AUTH** with the same methods plus **if-authenticated**. Account for **level 15 commands** with **start-stop** records to **ISE-GROUP** on the **default** list.
steps.hint: `aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group ISE-GROUP local`, `aaa authorization exec VTY-AUTH group ISE-GROUP local if-authenticated`, `aaa accounting commands 15 default start-stop group ISE-GROUP`.

commands.cmd: aaa authentication login VTY-AUTH group ISE-GROUP local
commands.note: Logins try ISE first and use local accounts only when ISE can't be reached.
commands.explain: Creates a login method list: try ISE first, and fall back to local accounts only if ISE can't be reached.

commands.cmd: aaa authorization exec VTY-AUTH group ISE-GROUP local if-authenticated
commands.note: ISE decides whether the user gets an EXEC shell and at what privilege level.
commands.explain: Asks ISE whether the user may start a shell, with local fallback if already authenticated.

commands.cmd: aaa accounting commands 15 default start-stop group ISE-GROUP
commands.note: Every privilege 15 command is logged to ISE.
commands.explain: Sends a record of every level 15 command to ISE, so changes are logged centrally.

steps.title: Apply the lists to the VTY lines
steps.learn: Named method lists do nothing until a line uses them. The **default** lists apply automatically to every line that doesn't name one, which is why the accounting list needed no line command.
steps.task: On **line vty 0 4**, use **VTY-AUTH** for login authentication and for EXEC authorization.

commands.explain: Enters configuration for the VTY lines.
Uses the VTY-AUTH method list for logins on these lines.

commands.note: SSH logins to R1 now go to ISE.
commands.explain: Uses the VTY-AUTH method list to authorize the shell on these lines.

steps.title: Predict the fallback
steps.learn: Getting fallback right is what keeps you from locking yourself out, or from leaving a back door open.
steps.question: ISE is up, and it **rejects** the username admin because the account was disabled in Active Directory. What does R1 do?

options.text: Refuses the login. A reject from ISE is final, and the local method isn't tried.
Tries the local admin account next and logs the user in.
options.why: The next method is tried only when the server doesn't respond. A reject (FAIL) ends the list.

options.text: Lets the user in because of if-authenticated.
options.why: `if-authenticated` is about authorization after a successful login, not about authentication.

summary: AAA with a TACACS+ server and server group pointing at ISE, login and EXEC authorization method lists with local fallback applied to the VTY lines, and command accounting for privilege 15.
